overview: This Senate resolution commends the American Chemical Society, a scientific organization founded by 35 chemists in New York in 1876, on its 150th anniversary. It recognizes the society's contributions to American science, education and the economy through research, publications and programs, and notes that Congress chartered it in 1938. The resolution also affirms the importance of science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) education and encourages young people to pursue careers in chemistry and related fields. Copies are to be sent to the society's leaders. It is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on April 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say honoring a long-standing scientific organization highlights the role chemistry plays in health, industry and innovation and encourages students to enter the field.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
